title: Final Frozen Evaluation

final_model.training_strategy: SMOTE applied to training data only
final_model.threshold_selection: Selected on validation data only. Test data was not used for threshold selection.

important_findings: SMOTE improved validation AP relative to the unweighted LightGBM reference.
SMOTE achieved slightly higher frozen test AP than the unweighted LightGBM reference.
Class weighting degraded both validation and frozen test ranking performance.
Platt scaling substantially improved probability calibration.
Platt scaling preserved AP and ROC-AUC because it is a monotonic probability transformation.
Operational thresholds were selected using validation data only.
The final test set remained untouched during threshold selection.
Equal-width risk bands are sparse after calibration and should not be interpreted as naturally monotonic risk categories.
V1-V28 are PCA-derived/anonymized variables, so SHAP explanations report model influence without assigning business semantics.
limitations: The frozen test set contains only 52 fraud cases.
Risk-band statistics are therefore sparse and unstable at the upper bands.
The dataset is historical and highly imbalanced.
PCA-derived features limit direct business interpretation.
SMOTE creates synthetic training examples and may not perfectly represent future fraud patterns.
The system has not yet been evaluated in a live production environment.
